messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH memory pressure on runtime-prod-3 (gpu-pool-c). Multiple GPU OOM events across replicas. Affected service: runtime-inference-v2. Rate spike at 2026-03-15T09:07Z. Auto-escalation to oncall. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2418004321 :rotating_light:

maria: ack — I'm taking this. oncall for infra today. starting live triage.

jas: pinging in from next shift, can take handoff in 20 if needed. do we have customer impact yet?

ops-bot: Customer-impact-summary: 3 tenants showing increased 5xx (model timeout/oom), 90th latency doubled for affected routes, ~1.8% overall error rate across region-us-east-1. No full outage.

maria: good to know — immediate mitigations: 1) throttle incoming bursts, 2) reduce default max_batch_tokens for runtime-prod-3 to 256, 3) enable kvcache-eviction aggressive mode for pool-c. doing 2 & 3 now.

maria: executing quick config change (rolling) — using control plane API: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/pools/runtime-prod-3/config 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
  -d '{"max_batch_tokens":256, "kvcache_eviction":"aggressive"}'
```

maria: API response: 200 OK — rolling update started.

liam: can someone grab nvidia-smi and runtime memory stats from one of the affected pods? want to see if this is fragmentation vs single large alloc.

maria: grabbing logs now. kubectl commands: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/runtime-inference-v2-7f6d --since=10m | tail -n 200
kubectl -n inference exec -it runtime-inference-v2-7f6d -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,memory.free --format=csv
```

maria: nvidia-smi output (snippet):
```
index, name, memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB], memory.free [MiB]
0, A100-SXM4-40GB, 40960 MiB, 38912 MiB, 2048 MiB
```

maria: runtime logs show repeated allocation failure messages: 
```
2026-03-15T09:08:45Z ERROR runtime::memory: allocation failed: request 20480 bytes, free contiguous 16384 bytes, total free 2.0GiB, frag_ratio=0.42
2026-03-15T09:08:45Z WARN  runtime::kvcache: insert failed, evicted 0 entries, current_entries=142398
```

anya: looks like high fragmentation + kvcache growth. hypothesis: long-tail keys + big prompt prefixes caused kvcache to fill with large entries so contiguous blocks shrink -> allocation fails for new attention tensors. immediate mitigations seem correct.

liam: agree. Two quick asks: 1) reduce worker concurrency per GPU on pool-c by 1 to reduce peak simultaneous allocs, 2) rotate to smaller model variant for high-ttl tenants.

maria: lowering concurrency — updating pool config now: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/pools/runtime-prod-3/config 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
  -d '{"workers_per_gpu":3}'
```

maria: done — nodes are rejoining. telemetry shows drop in 95p alloc failures within 30s. :thumbsup:

david: uploading collected logs + shorttimeline: https://paste.redwood.internal/2418004321/logs — timeline in the paste:
- 09:06:58Z rate spike (ingress x2 normal)
- 09:07:10Z first allocation failure on replica-a
- 09:08:30Z OOM kill on replica-b
- 09:09:00Z auto-throttle triggered by LB
- 09:10:12Z rolling config changes (batch_tokens down, eviction on)
- 09:12:00Z errors fall but still occasional retries

maria: partial logs from replica-b OOM: 
```
[09:08:29Z] runtime.error: GPU out-of-memory while allocating attention cache, required 4.0MiB, contiguous_available 0.0MiB
[09:08:29Z] kernel: slab_map: high fragment counts: slab_free_chunks=102, slab_largest_free=0.0MiB
```

anya: note for RCA: need KV key-size distribution and top prefixes. can we export kvcache metadata for last 24h. I'll run a script to sample keys and sizes. hypothesis: a small set of very large prompts pushed contiguous allocation needs.

jas: are customers seeing degraded quality from fallback/resize? any SLA hits?

ops-bot: Impact update: 3 tenants saw transient retries, 0 customers reported data loss. SLA alert: elevated latency for ~14 minutes for affected routes.

maria: we also pinned affected tenant routes to redwood-mini-v1 (smaller model) as a protective measure for 2 customers. doing a gradual pin to avoid mass churn.

liam: we'll need a follow-up action list:
- collect kvcache key-size histogram (anya)
- add eviction heuristics for long-lived large entries (runtime team)
- improve contiguous allocator compaction / defrag heuristic (runtime team)
- add autoscaling rule: if frag_ratio > 0.3 and alloc_fail_rate > 5/m -> scale up or throttle (sre/product)
- postmortem + customer comms (maria + support)

david: opening ticket INF-8932 for tracking RCA and owners. linking logs & cfg diffs.

maria: monitoring now. since config changes, 5xx rate down from 1.8% to 0.12%, 95p latency trending back to baseline. will leave incident open for 3h and then close when stable. :spiral_note_pad:

anya: ran quick kv sample: top 20 keys account for 64% of kvcache bytes, average entry size for top 5 is ~1.2MiB. attaching CSV to ticket.

liam: that's a smoking gun. long-lived big entries + burst concurrency = fragmentation. For immediate next-week work: we should add per-key size caps + LRU-weighted by size.

maria: thanks all. handoff to jas in 20. jas please take final monitor until close.

jas: taking it. will watch for 3h window then verify tickets. if anything spikes I'll escalate. :eyes:

incident-bot: Incident 2418004321 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Primary hypothesis: KV cache large-entry fragmentation causing allocation failures. Actions: throttles, batch_size reduction, eviction aggressive, concurrency reduction, tenant model pin. Follow-ups assigned in INF-8932.

maria: closing notes to add to postmortem: immediate mitigations worked; root cause likely combined kvcache size skew + bursty concurrency; long-term fixes: compaction/defrag, per-key caps, smarter eviction, autoscale triggers. I'll draft postmortem and customer comms after shift.
